title: Runtime Tradecraft: Pocket Deck for Ops & Sellers
summary: Compact slide pack for technical sellers and ops to run fast pilot conversations that emphasize runtime tradeoffs (latency, cost, reliability) and pragmatic fallbacks. Includes 30s/60s hooks, pilot checklist, demo script, and objection scripts for common procurement/security questions.

Cover: Runtime Tradecraft — Pocket Deck for Ops & Sellers
Asha Menon (SE Lead) • Draft ‥
One-liner: Help customers pick an inference strategy that balances latency, unit cost, and reliability without overpromising.
Use: 8-12 minute field briefing + leave-behind for platform teams.

TL;DR for busy engineering buyers
- Redwood offers three serving modes (Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private) with unified API and rollout primitives.
- Decision lens: latency SLO, token economics, data isolation/controls.
- Quick ask: run a 2-week pilot using our pilot template to quantify tail latency and per-token cost on representative traffic.

Target personas & conversation mapping
- Integration Architect / Platform Engineer: cares about routing policies, fallbacks, and component isolation. Bring: routing-policy cheat sheet + canary checklist.
- Product/ML Engineer: cares about quality drift, KV cache benefits. Bring: eval prompts and sample token-cost projection.
- Procurement/Security: cares about data residency, KMS/HSM. Bring: private deployment checklist and compliance artifacts.

30s / 60s seller hooks (scripts)
- 30s hook for platform engineer: "We map your SLOs to three runtime levers — routing policy (region/variant), batching & cache, and quantization profile — and show expected cost/latency delta within 48h using a synthetic replay."
- 60s hook for product lead: "We’ll run a low-friction pilot that measures user-facing latency histogram, token spend per request, and model quality regression on your prompts — then recommend the cheapest config that meets your SLOs."

Runtime tradeoffs cheat sheet (one pager)
- Batching: lowers per-token cost, increases p99 latency; good for high-throughput async jobs.
- KV / prefix cache: improves latency and reduces compute for repeated context.
- Quantization: saves cost, minor quality delta for retrieval/QA; test with eval set.
- Fallbacks: cheaper model variant for capacity/surge; automated routing + fallback rollout policy keeps apps up.
- Dedicated vs Hosted: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation; Hosted is fastest to ship.

Pilot checklist (2-week quick pilot)
- Week 0: setup access, choose 5000-10k representative queries, map SLOs and success metrics.
- Week 1: run parallel replay across two configs (latency-optimized, cost-optimized). Capture histograms, token counts, and output quality ratings (sampled).
- Week 2: analyze results, run a canary on production traffic path with routing policy, recommend final config and estimated monthly run rate.
- Deliverables: 1-page cost/latency chart, top 10 model regressions, canary rollback plan.

Demo script (5min deploy + 5min measurement)
- Step 1 (90s): Quick show of Redwood Console — route rule creation, per-route metrics, token-level cost.
- Step 2 (90s): Start replay job with two model profiles; show live dashboard of throughput and p50/p99 latency.
- Step 3 (2min): Snapshot results, run a simple eval on 20 prompt sets, flag quality diffs.
- Step 4 (1min): Show fallback in action: simulate spike, automatic route to cheaper variant and observed gracefulness.

Common objections & tight scripts
- Objection: "We can self-host cheaper." Script: "Self-hosting moves ops burden to you; we give predictable economics + observability for the same or lower TCO once you factor infra & SRE allocation. Ask: What’s your current ops cost per 100k tokens?"
- Objection: "We need on-prem for compliance." Script: "We support Private deployments with KMS/HSM integrations and an audit trail; we can ship a compliance checklist and run a tabletop in the pilot."
- Objection: "Latency at p99 matters." Script: "We treat p99 as a primary metric: show routing & burst capacity policies; run canary to validate tail behavior under realistic load."

Canary & rollback quick play
- Canary checklist: define canary % and duration, monitor p50/p99, error rate, quality deltas on sampled outputs.
- Automated rollback triggers: sustained p99 > SLO + error rate spike > 2x baseline OR quality regression above threshold on labeled prompts.
- Triage steps: isolate route, switch to fallback model variant, notify on-call, rollback config, escalate to R&D if regression persists.

Success metrics we recommend collecting
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end (including network).
- Cost: tokens per request, total tokens/day, estimated monthly spend at projected RPS.
- Quality: sampled BLEU/ROUGE where relevant + human-rating panel for 100 requests.
- Reliability: successful requests %, fallback activations, mean time to recovery for incidents.

Appendix: quick prompt/eval templates (copyable)
- Customer support summarization: 50 example tickets + rubric for preservation of intent + hallucination check.
- Search-rerank: top-10 candidates with NDCG sample scoring.
- Safety smoke tests: prompts that trigger policy-sensitive content, expectation: safe fallback or sanitized output.
- Token-cost projection snippet: formula and example for monthly burn given average tokens/request and RPS.

Next steps & playbook for sellers (two-liner checklist)
- Quick-qualify: confirm SLOs, data residency, current throughput, success metric priority.
- Offer: 2-week pilot with pre-baked replay + console access; include one on-call hour for canary day.
- Follow-up: deliver 1-page recommendation + 30-min review with engineering stakeholders.
- Ask to include in follow-up email: sample prompts, access instructions, and Confluence pilot page link.
